subject: Prospect questions: service-execution ports, subprocessors, and deletion timelines
messages:
From: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@ledger.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Jun 2028 14:22:00 -0400
Subject: Quick Qs for POC — where does data run / who sees it?

Hi Logan,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — LedgerAI’s compliance team needs a short write-up so we can scope the POC:

- Where exactly are inference requests executed for the hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private? Which regions / cloud providers?
- Do any Redwood subprocessors (monitoring, logging, telemetry) receive raw or token-level request data, or only metadata? If so, where are those subprocessors located?
- Does KV / prefix caching ever get persisted to disk or cross-region replicated?
- What parts of request lifecycle (control plane vs data plane) might cross borders (e.g., EU -> US) for monitoring or billing?
- Deletion expectations: if we request immediate deletion for a user’s data, what is the timeline for (a) runtime cache, (b) long-term backups, and (c) audit logs?

Can you attach a simple processing map and subprocessor inventory we can hand to legal? We’re trying to confirm we don’t need an additional addendum for cross-border processing.

Appreciate a short summary and any artifacts.

—Alex
Alex Moreno
Head of Infrastructure
LedgerAI
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@ledger.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 16 Jun 2028 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick Qs for POC — where does data run / who sees it?

Alex — thanks for the clear list. Quick overview below; attaching a compact processing map and subprocessor inventory for legal review.

Summary (short):
- Data plane (inference execution) is region-configurable. For hosted customers we default to the nearest available region (US: us-east-1). For Dedicated you get reserved pools in the requested region (we can pin to us-east-1). Private deployments keep everything inside your VPC / on-prem.
- Control plane (metadata, job orchestration, billing metering) runs in our control region (us-east-1). Control-plane traffic is limited to management metadata; we do not send model inputs/outputs to the control plane for processing.
- Subprocessors: primary cloud providers (AWS, GCP) for compute/storage, monitoring (Datadog), S3-compatible object stores for persisted artifacts, and a limited telemetry pipeline for aggregated metrics. The attached CSV lists locations and roles.
- Caching: KV/prefix cache lives in GPU host memory and local NVMe scratch for batching; by default it is ephemeral and not cross-region replicated. If you enable disk-backed persistent caching (opt-in), it is stored in customer-designated regional storage.
- Cross-border hops: For hosted customers in the EU we route data to eu-west regions where available; however some telemetry/metrics (aggregated traces, error sampling) are collected by our monitoring subprocessor and may be routed to our control plane in the US unless you select EU-only evidence (available on Dedicated/Private).

Deletion timelines (default hosted):
- Runtime cache / KV: immediate eviction on request; in-flight tokens dropped within seconds (0–60s typical).
- Persistent storage / object artifacts: forced deletion initiated within 24 hours; reclaimed from active storage within 30 days (default snapshot retention).
- Backups / snapshots: rotated and purged according to retention windows — default 30 days, with secure purge thereafter.
- Audit logs: retained for 90 days by default (can be shortened or extended in contract). Audit log deletion is subject to legal hold exceptions.

Notes / mitigations for cross-border concerns:
- For POC we recommend Dedicated region pinning to us-east-1 to avoid EU->US telemetry hops.
- Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) removes control-plane telemetry from your tenancy and gives you full custody over backups.
- We can add contractual language limiting telemetry export and guaranteeing regional residency for a defined set of artifacts (we do this in enterprise SOWs).

Attached: redwood_processing_map_202806.pdf, redwood_subprocessors_2028.csv (summary inventory). If useful I can loop in our security engineer for a short call.

Best,
Logan Wright
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@ledger.ai>
Cc: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 17 Jun 2028 10:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Quick Qs for POC — where does data run / who sees it?

Alex — quick technical clarifications (adding a couple of operational details you’ll want to pass to infra):

> On Sat, Jun 16, 2028 at 09:08 AM Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com> wrote:
> > - Caching: KV/prefix cache lives in GPU host memory and local NVMe scratch for batching; by default it is ephemeral and not cross-region replicated.
>
- Ephemeral caches are wiped on container termination; nothing is snapshot to object storage unless you opt-in for persistent caching.
- If you use the hosted API and traffic is routed through regional edge proxies there is a short-lived TLS-terminated hop at the edge (we do TLS to the cluster) — payloads are not persisted at the edge beyond ephemeral memory.
- Network ports: inference egress is standard HTTPS (443) to model containers; observability agents make outbound connections to monitoring endpoints (Datadog) on 443/8125 depending on transport. I’ve attached a tiny netflow_ports.txt listing ports you may need to allow in a restricted environment.

Operational recommendation for LedgerAI POC:
1) Provision a Dedicated pool in us-east-1 and pin the model to that pool.
2) Turn off disk-backed caching.
3) Request our EU-data handling addendum only if you plan to send EU-rooted customer data through hosted EU regions — otherwise Dedicated us-east keeps traffic in-region.

Attachment: netflow_ports.txt (ports summary).

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
From: Alex Moreno <alex.moreno@ledger.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, procurement@ledger.ai
Date: Mon, 18 Jun 2028 15:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Quick Qs for POC — where does data run / who sees it?

Thanks Logan / Marissa — that’s helpful. A couple quick follow-ups before we loop legal:

- Can you put the deletion SLAs and the telemetry-evidence routing promise into an interim one-page addendum we can attach to the SOW?
- For audit logs: can you commit to a 30-day deletion default for this POC (instead of 90) and confirm whether log entries contain any raw prompt text or are they metadata-only?
- Can you share a DocuSign link or a simple checkbox template (we prefer a short clause we can sign via DocuSign) that covers region pinning + telemetry restriction for the POC?

If you can send the one-pager and the DocuSign link I’ll get procurement to sign and we’ll schedule the Dedicated pool reservation.

Appreciate it — Alex
